what_its_for: Belzutifan is a cancer medicine used to treat adults with certain kidney tumors, a genetic condition called Von Hippel-Lindau (VHL) disease that causes tumors in the kidneys, brain, or pancreas, and a type of advanced kidney cancer called clear cell renal cell carcinoma that has been treated before with other cancer medicines.
how_to_take: Swallow the tablet whole with or without food. Take it at the same time each day. Do not crush, chew, or break the tablet. If you vomit after taking a dose, do not take another dose that day — just take your next dose at the regular scheduled time.
dosing: The usual adult dose is 120 mg (three 40 mg tablets) taken by mouth once daily. Your doctor may lower your dose or ask you to stop temporarily if you have side effects. Always follow the dose your doctor prescribes — do not change it on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose and it has been less than 12 hours since your scheduled time, take it as soon as you remember. If it has been more than 12 hours, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. Never take two doses at once to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store belzutifan at room temperature between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it in its original container with the lid tightly closed. Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not flush medicines down the toilet — ask your pharmacist about proper medicine disposal.
what_to_avoid: Avoid becoming pregnant while taking this medicine, as it can harm an unborn baby. Use effective birth control during treatment and for at least 1 week after your last dose. Do not breastfeed during treatment or for at least 1 week after your last dose. Avoid driving or operating heavy machinery if you feel dizzy or tired, as this medicine can cause low red blood cell counts (anemia) and dizziness. Talk to your doctor or pharmacist before starting any new medicines, vitamins, or herbal supplements, as some may interact with belzutifan.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away if you experience: severe shortness of breath, difficulty breathing, or feel like you cannot get enough air (these may be signs of low oxygen levels); unusual tiredness or weakness; dizziness or lightheadedness; fast or irregular heartbeat; severe headache; vision changes; swelling in your hands or feet; signs of infection such as fever or chills; if you are pregnant or think you might be pregnant; or if any side effects become severe or do not go away.
when_it_works: Belzutifan works by blocking a protein called HIF-2 alpha that helps cancer cells grow and survive. By blocking this protein, it slows or stops tumor growth. It may take several months before you or your doctor can tell if the medicine is working. Blood tests and scans will be done regularly to check your progress. Do not stop taking it without talking to your doctor first, even if you feel well.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: This medicine can cause serious harm to an unborn baby. Women who can become pregnant must use effective birth control during treatment and for at least 1 week after stopping. Men with female partners who can become pregnant should also use birth control during treatment and for at least 1 week after the last dose. Do not breastfeed during treatment or for 1 week after the last dose. Kidney or liver problems: Tell your doctor if you have kidney or liver problems, as your dose may need to be adjusted. Older adults: Older patients may be more sensitive to side effects, so extra monitoring may be needed. Children: This medicine is not approved for use in children.
